rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: A manager gives specific, honest praise to a newcomer who doubts themself, naming what was done well. Vague praise is discounted, and concrete feedback offers something the doubting mind can accept.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: When a task goes well, the person credits luck, the team or an easy assignment. Praise is filed away as a mistake in others' judgment, while any error is taken as proof.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: The person compares their inside doubts with colleagues' outside confidence and stays silent in meetings. Silence then makes them less visible, which feeds the belief they add little.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: A senior colleague notices a capable newcomer who never speaks in meetings. Inviting their view, sharing that everyone once felt lost and giving specific credit help them find a voice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: The person asks a basic question and the reply is kind and matter-of-fact. The feared humiliation does not arrive, and the belief that ignorance must be hidden starts to loosen.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: The person keeps a list of completed work and positive feedback and reads it when doubt spikes. Testing the thought against facts is more effective than trying to feel confident.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: Confidence grows as competence does, and the person accepts that not knowing everything is normal. They begin to help the next newcomer, which cements their own sense of belonging.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
rows.subtype: Stage 1: The news and the glow [Actor]
rows.description: A well-liked engineer is made team lead and feels proud and validated after years of effort. Family and friends congratulate, and the rise in status feels like a reward earned.

rows.subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
rows.description: The new lead starts to see themself as the smart one, quotes their own past decisions and enjoys deference. Praise slowly turns into an expectation of it.
graph_context: previous stage: The news and the glow
next stage: Distance from former peers

rows.subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
rows.description: The lead skips lunches with old friends, talks down to them and shares less. Some distance is natural in a new role, but a sense of being above them is not.
